1
Which quantity with its unit is correct?
A
acceleration of a bicycle = 1.4 m s–1
B
electric current in a lamp = 0.25 A s–1
C
electric potential difference across a battery = 8.0 J C–1
D
kinetic energy of a car = 4500 N m–1

hints: Look at the unit attached to acceleration of $1.4 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and ask whether $\text{m s}^{-1}$ measures velocity or rate of change of velocity.
Recall the defining relations $V = W/Q$ for potential difference and $I = Q/t$ for current, so check what $\text{J C}^{-1}$ and $\text{A s}^{-1}$ simplify to.
Recall that work and all forms of energy have unit joule $\text{J} = \text{N m}$, so compare $4500 \text{ N m}^{-1}$ with $\text{N m}$.
walkthrough: List the four quantity-unit pairs: acceleration in $\text{m s}^{-1}$, current in $\text{A s}^{-1}$, potential difference in $\text{J C}^{-1}$, kinetic energy in $\text{N m}^{-1}$.

Use definitions: acceleration $a = \Delta v/\Delta t$ has unit $\text{m s}^{-2}$, current $I = Q/t$ has unit $\text{A}$, potential difference $V = W/Q$ has unit $\text{J C}^{-1} = \text{V}$, energy has unit $\text{J} = \text{N m}$.
Compare each: $\text{m s}^{-1}$ is velocity not acceleration, $\text{A s}^{-1}$ is $\text{C s}^{-2}$ not current, $\text{N m}^{-1}$ is force per length not energy.
Check $\text{J C}^{-1}$: since $V = W/Q$, $1 \text{ V} = 1 \text{ J}$ per $1 \text{ C}$, so $8.0 \text{ J C}^{-1} = 8.0 \text{ V}$ is a valid potential difference for a battery.
Only the potential difference pairing matches its defining unit. This is option C.

A.explanation: Acceleration is rate of change of velocity, so its unit is $\text{m s}^{-2}$, not $\text{m s}^{-1}$ which is the unit of velocity.

B.explanation: Electric current is charge per unit time with unit ampere $\text{A}$, so $\text{A s}^{-1}$ is charge per time squared and is incorrect.

C.explanation: Potential difference is $V = W/Q$, so $1 \text{ V} = 1 \text{J C}^{-1}$, making $8.0 \text{ J C}^{-1}$ correct.

D.explanation: Kinetic energy is measured in joules where $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ N m}$, so $\text{N m}^{-1}$ is force per length and is incorrect.
